title: Tryouts and Mixtape
premise: Coral Zhou, a debate champion who can't win the argument at home, has spent ten years being so careful it hurts—careful about his immigrant parents' expectations, careful about his best friend Priya's fragile loyalty, careful never to want anything too loudly. When his English teacher pairs him with his nemesis, the effortlessly popular Theo Vance, for a semester-long oral history project, Coral's invisibility strategy collapses: Theo wants to record the school's untold stories, including Coral's own. As the mixtape of voices grows, so does Coral's courage to speak—and when he finally tells the truth about his family and his feelings for Theo, it costs him Priya's friendship on the eve of prom. In the end, Coral learns that belonging built on silence was never belonging at all, and that some friendships, like some arguments, are worth losing to be heard.
about_author: Yara Montrose is a former high-school debate coach who now writes stories about teenagers finding their voices in noisy rooms. She lives in a coastal town with an unreasonable number of houseplants and a dog named Rebuttal.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Careful
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. We meet Coral mid-debate tournament, winning flawlessly, then flinching through dinner as his parents argue over his future in two languages. He catalogs all the ways he stays small at home and school. Emotional beat: the ache of being excellent everywhere except where it matters.

chapters.title: Assigned Seating
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Ms. Okafor pairs Coral with Theo Vance—the boy who mocked his accent freshman year—for a semester-long oral history project. Coral protests; she doesn't budge. Their first meeting is barbed, but Theo surprises him by proposing they record real people's real stories. Beat: reluctant curiosity under old resentment.

chapters.title: First Recording
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral/Theo POV. They interview the night custodian, Mr. Delgado, whose story of crossing borders mirrors Coral's parents' in ways he's never said aloud. Theo listens differently than Coral expected. Beat: the first crack in Coral's armor; Theo sees something true in him.

chapters.title: Priya Knows Best
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Priya notices Coral spending lunches with Theo and warns him—Theo's crowd destroyed her reputation last year. Coral defends the project; Priya calls it betrayal. At home, his mother finds his recorder and assumes he's hiding worse things. Beat: pressure closing in from both sides.

chapters.title: Mixtape, Side A
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo reveals why he started the project: his older brother's voice, preserved on old tapes after his death, taught him that recording someone is a way of keeping them. He asks Coral what he'd say if no one were listening. Beat: intimacy deepens; Coral almost tells the truth and swerves.

chapters.title: The Argument at Home
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral's father discovers the project includes an interview about the family restaurant's struggles and forbids him to air their private life. For once, Coral argues back—and loses, because winning means wounding them. Beat: the cost of voice made concrete; Coral records a confession tape he doesn't share.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A classmate plays Coral's private confession tape—his fears about his family, his confused feelings for Theo—at a party. The school buzzes; Priya admits she told the host where to find it. Beat: humiliation, fury, and the sick clarity that silence protected no one.

chapters.title: What the Tape Couldn't Say
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral confronts Priya, then his parents, playing them the full unedited recording—his love, his fear, his ten years of carefulness. His mother says nothing; his father walks out. Theo offers to pull the project; Coral refuses. Beat: the lowest point becomes the turning point—he chooses truth over safety.

chapters.title: Prom, Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On prom night, instead of attending, Coral and Theo stage the oral history as a public listening event in the gym—every voice, including Coral's family's, played raw. His father arrives mid-playback and hears himself honored, not exposed. Priya comes, and doesn't forgive him yet. Beat: climax—belonging rebuilt on honesty, not performance.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Weeks later: Coral and his father cook together in imperfect truce; Priya sends a single text—working on it. Theo hands Coral a new blank tape labeled 'you, next.' Coral presses record and starts speaking without rehearsing. Beat: resolution—Coral stops being careful and starts being heard.
